claim: For the real two-dimensional Cesàro space \(\mathrm{ces}_2^{(2)}\), with \(\|(x,y)\|=\bigl(|x|^2+((|x|+|y|)/2)^2\bigr)^{1/2}\), the Banach--Mazur distance to the Euclidean plane is exactly \(d_{\mathrm{BM}}(\mathrm{ces}_2^{(2)},\ell_2^2)=\sqrt{1+1/\sqrt5}\).

correctness.rationale: The published linear normalization expands exactly to \(N_a(u,v)^2=u^2+v^2+2a|uv|\) with \(a=1/\sqrt5\). The Euclidean disk gives the upper factor \(\sqrt{1+a}\). For any inner ellipse \(E_A\), containment in both quadratic branches forces \((p-1)(q-1)\ge(r-a)^2\) and \((p-1)(q-1)\ge(r+a)^2\), hence \(\max\{p,q\}\ge1+a\). Since both coordinate unit vectors belong to the unit ball, any outer homothety factor satisfies \(\lambda^2\ge\max\{p,q\}\). The upper and lower bounds coincide.

value.rationale: The object is a classical Cesàro sequence space with a substantial geometric literature, and Banach--Mazur distance to \(\ell_2^2\) is a canonical isomorphic invariant. The value is exact, nontrivial, and comes with a sharp all-ellipses lower bound rather than a coordinate-comparison estimate. The proof also isolates a reusable exact lemma for the natural normalized family \(N_a^2=u^2+v^2+2a|uv|\).
